surprises: Table alias shadows the struct column: SELECT a.* FROM test4 AS a does TABLE-star expansion (columns a, b), not struct-field expansion — the alias wins, silently.
COUNT(a.*) is silently rewritten to count_star() and returns 3, counting the NULL-struct row; it is not a struct-aware count.
EXCLUDE/REPLACE name matching is case-insensitive even for double-quoted identifiers: EXCLUDE("J") removes j, EXCLUDE("weird name") removes "Weird Name".
REPLACE(expr AS I) renames the output column to the alias's exact case 'I' while still matching field i — output name comes from the alias, not the struct.
Only the bare two-part form parses: test.a.* and (a).* are both parser errors.
EXCLUDE of all fields errors ONLY if the whole select list ends up empty; with another select item present the star contributes zero columns with no error.
a.* is accepted in GROUP BY and ORDER BY (expanding to fields), while WHERE rejects it at parse time with a hint to use COLUMNS(*).
summary: a.* on a STRUCT(i,j) column expands in-place to bare, unqualified field names in declaration order, with types from the struct; a NULL struct row yields NULL in every expanded field (identical output to SELECT a.i, a.j). EXCLUDE/REPLACE match field names case-insensitively — even double-quoted — but a REPLACE alias's exact case becomes the output column name, and REPLACE expressions may reference other columns of the table. Resolution order matters: if a table alias with the same name exists, the alias wins and a.* becomes a table star; struct-star only applies when no such table binding exists, and only the two-part form a.* parses (test.a.* and (a).* are syntax errors). Error pins: non-struct column gives 'Cannot extract field from expression \"a.*\" because it is not a struct'; unknown EXCLUDE/REPLACE names give 'Column \"x\" in EXCLUDE/REPLACE list not found in a'; a fully-emptied select list gives 'SELECT list is empty after resolving * expressions!' (but excluding all fields is fine if other select items remain). a.* is parse-rejected in WHERE ('STAR expression is not allowed in the WHERE clause. Use COLUMNS(*) instead.') yet accepted in GROUP BY/ORDER BY, and COUNT(a.*) silently becomes count_star(). Python-side: fetchall returns dicts/None, pandas dtype object, arrow type struct<i: int32, j: int32>.
